paper_metadata.title: QuanFraud: Quantum State Veriﬁcation Scheme for Fraud Detection in IoT-Assisted Quantum-Blockchain Networks

summary: The paper proposes QuanFraud, a hybrid IoT–quantum‑blockchain fraud‑detection pipeline combining GHZ‑θ state verification and QSVC-based quantum ML. On a 20,468‑record financial dataset with 117 features, the QSVC model achieves only 42.1% ± 2.8% balanced accuracy (Recall 0.625, F1 0.6524), far below classical baselines such as Random Forest and XGBoost (>77% BA), with the authors emphasizing verifiability and auditability rather than predictive performance.

experiments.description: GHZ-θ quantum state verification on a 4-qubit GHZ state for IoT device/channel integrity, including preparation, fidelity checking, and pass/fail validation.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One qubit per participant/device in a 4-party GHZ instantiation; the state is prepared as (|0000⟩+|1111⟩)/√2.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Verify whether the distributed entangled state remains close to an ideal GHZ state and accept only if fidelity exceeds threshold.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: θ-protocol acceptance test with fidelity threshold F >= 0.5; abort on disturbance.

problem_instance.description: Four-party GHZ verification for IoT-assisted quantum-blockchain network roles (sensor, gateway, validator, auditor).

dataset_specification.description: 4-qubit GHZ instantiation; roles mapped to q1-q4.

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Measurement outcomes and fidelity/pass-fail distributions reported for the 4-qubit GHZ state.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Fidelity estimation and valid/not valid classification of GHZ states; on-chain logging of state verification metadata.

speedup_claims.caveats: No speedup claim is made for GHZ-theta verification; the paper only states the preparation is practical on NISQ devices and uses O(n) gates/qubits.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(n) gates/qubits for GHZ preparation; verification described as practical on NISQ devices

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not designed as a computational speedup experiment; uses a 4‑qubit GHZ state verification circuit.
limiting_factors: No classical comparison or computational benchmark
Purpose is protocol verification rather than algorithmic advantage

notes: Hardware inferred as real_qpu_superconducting because the paper explicitly states 'In IBM Quantum' for GHZ fidelity estimation and uses IBM Qiskit; no specific device name is given.
Circuit depth not numerically reported; only the GHZ preparation steps (Hadamard + CNOT cascade) are described.
No asymptotic speedup claim is made for this verification experiment.
The GHZ–θ protocol experiment is used only for channel/state verification in the architecture.
The paper does not claim computational advantage or compare against classical verification methods.

experiments.description: Quantum fraud classification using QSVC with ZZ-FeatureMap and a trainable RY/RZ/CX ansatz on PCA/SMOTE-processed financial fraud data.

algorithm.variant: QSVC with ZZFeatureMap kernel embedding (with optional VQC optimization layer)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical features are reduced by PCA and embedded into a 4-qubit ZZFeatureMap; the paper also mentions amplitude encoding and angle re-uploading as considered variants, but the implemented pipeline centers on ZZFeatureMap/QSVC.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary fraud classification (fraud / non-fraud) with calibrated scores and thresholding.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: SMOTE for class imbalance; nested CV with leakage-safe preprocessing; threshold K* selected on inner folds; calibration via Platt/Isotonic.

problem_instance.description: Financial fraud detection on an IoT-assisted quantum-blockchain pipeline.

dataset_specification.description: 20,468 records, 117 features; class imbalance approximately 27% positive / 73% negative; PCA and SMOTE applied; DID wallet metadata merged into sample.csv.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Normalization, PCA dimensionality reduction, SMOTE oversampling, clustering with K-Means in Algorithm 1, feature construction from PCA components and temporal attributes, leakage-safe train-only fitting, nested cross-validation.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Nested stratified 10-fold cross-validation with 5 inner folds; metrics include BA, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, Recall, F1; confidence intervals via DeLong and BCa bootstrap.

implementation_details.classical_solver: QSVC with classical calibration; classical baselines include Random Forest and XGBoost
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: PCA, SMOTE, normalization, K-Means clustering, train/test splitting, nested cross-validation, calibration.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Thresholding at 0.75; Platt/Isotonic calibration; on-chain logging of scores and decisions.
implementation_details.total_execution_time: ~45 s end-to-end (paper-reported for the full pipeline)
classical_baselines: classical SVM (RBF kernel referenced as comparison)

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical baselines (Random Forest, XGBoost, classical SVM)
speedup_claims.conditions: NISQ constraints; the paper emphasizes verifiability and auditability rather than speedup
speedup_claims.caveats: No quantum advantage or speedup is claimed; classical baselines achieve higher balanced accuracy. The paper reports a practical end-to-end runtime of about 45 s, but not a speedup versus a matched classical runtime.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Polynomial in n and d for QSVC/VQC; GHZ preparation O(n) gates/qubits; overall pipeline time complexity O(n·m^2 + n + p) as stated
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(n^2) for classical SVMs (as stated in the paper)
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_quantum: ~45 s end-to-end for the full pipeline

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Only ~4 qubits used for feature embedding; shallow ZZFeatureMap + small variational circuit.
limiting_factors: Classical baselines (Random Forest, XGBoost) exceed ~77% balanced accuracy
Kernel estimation noise and limited feature embedding capacity

notes: Hardware type inferred as simulator_other because the paper states the qubits were validated on the IBM Qiskit simulator for QSVC, while IBM Quantum is mentioned separately for GHZ fidelity estimation.
The paper does not report a numeric circuit depth or transpiled depth for the QSVC circuit; only shallow/NISQ-friendly structure and gate types are described.
No optimizer name or variational parameter count is explicitly reported for the QSVC/VQC circuit.
The abstract explicitly states classical baselines achieve >77% balanced accuracy while QSVC yields 42.1 ± 2.8%.
Authors explicitly acknowledge QSVC does not lead in accuracy and frame the contribution as 'verifiability and auditability' rather than performance advantage.

experiments.description: Variational Quantum Classifier (VQC) evaluation using the same PCA/SMOTE-processed fraud dataset and ZZFeatureMap embedding.

algorithm.ansatz: Parameterized RY/RZ rotations with CX entangling layers

key_results.details: Reported in Table VIII as calibrated class probability outputs from the VQC circuit
Nested 10-fold cross-validation identical to the QSVC experiment
